Blob.description: Data named by its content's hash.

Chain.description:
An ordered run of parts, such as a model's blocks, that may sit on one device or be divided
between devices at any boundary between two of them.

Each part's output feeds the next, so an edge joins each part to the next. Dividing a model
between devices is placing a chain's parts on more than one; only the edge at a division
crosses between them.

parts.description: The parts in order. At least 2, none replicable, none in another chain.

Dtype.description: What an edge carries: a tensor's element type, or opaque bytes (an encoded image, a record).

Edge.description: Data that moves from an input or a part to a part, or out of the job.

dtype.description: What the data is: a tensor's element type, or opaque bytes.

note.description: Free text: the author's reasons. mag never reads it.

release.description:
Whether the producing part releases this output, so that it may go where its local-only
inputs may not. Only a part releases; an input is never released.

to.description: A part, or `None` for a result of the job.

Input.description: Data a job reads from outside its parts.

local_only.description:
Never placed on a member marked remote, nor is anything computed from it unless a stage
releases it. The graph file must say it either way: left out, it is refused, so that
forgetting it never lets an input move.

Job.description:
A job's name, how much it weighs against the other jobs in the pool, and what it needs.

Beyond its need a job wants to run as fast as it can: when jobs share the pool, an
arrangement is judged by the sum over jobs of priority times each job's rate.

note.description: Free text: the author's reasons. mag never reads it.

priority.description: The job's weight against other jobs. At least 1.

Mark.description: How a part may be spread over devices.

oneOf.description: As many copies as there are devices to hold them, each pulling items from one queue.

Need.description:
What an arrangement must give a job. Each field is optional, and a job with neither only
wants to run as fast as its priority allows.

deadline_seconds.description: Seconds from its submission by which it must finish. Finite and above 0.

rate_per_second.description:
The rate it must sustain, in its own steps per second (items, tokens or optimiser
steps): a service's need. Finite and above 0.

Part.description:
The smallest piece mag places: a unit with the weights it holds, the memory it needs, and
where it can stop.

memory_bytes.description: The memory it needs on its device, weights and working memory together.

note.description: Free text: the author's reasons. mag never reads it.

pin.description: A member or a backend it must run on.

step.description: Where the part can stop with its state written out, to move or to make way.

tolerance.description: The numerics it accepts, which decide the devices it may run on.

unit.description: The function the part runs, already built into each member's binary.

weights.description: The weights it holds, fetched once per member and kept.

oneOf.description: On a device of this backend, so that results stay comparable.

Step.description: The point where a part can stop with its state written out.

oneOf.description: After each item, as a map stops.
After each token, as a decoder stops.
After each optimiser step, as a learner stops.
After each round of a loop.

Tolerance.description:
The numerics a part accepts. A device takes the part only if its measured bounds for the
part's operations meet it.

description:
One submitted job.

Every name in a graph (inputs, parts and chains together) is unique, and edges and chains
refer to inputs and parts by name. [`Graph::check`] says whether a graph is well formed.

chains.description: Ordered runs of parts that may be divided between devices at any part boundary.

edges.description: What moves between inputs and parts, and out of the job.

inputs.description: What the job reads from outside its parts.

job.description: The job's name, its weight and its need.

note.description: Free text: the author's reasons. mag never reads it.

parts.description: The pieces mag places. At least one.
